_comment: Where evidence lives once an entity is known. Discovery finds pages *about* a company; a page about a company is not the company. This file is shared by every lane: which paths a website keeps its case studies under, and which hosts carry a hiring board, is a fact about the web rather than about a product. A lane decides only which kinds it is missing.
probed: 2026-09 against 8 real company domains (slalom, thoughtworks, innowise, gravity9, softwaremill, factorhouse, taashee, sqldbm). Every entry below is here because it answered, and every removal is recorded with its reason.

discovery._comment: A sitemap is the only first-party surface that answered for every domain tested (8/8), and it names the real case-study and careers URLs instead of guessing at them. Guessing produced 200s that were the wrong *kind* of page (slalom's /case-studies redirects to 'Who we are'), and every domain serves a styled 404 carrying enough navigation chrome to fool a word count. Locate the sitemap first, then fetch the pages it names.

first_party_paths._comment: Fallbacks for a site whose sitemap is missing or thin. Ordered by how often each answered in the probe.

match._comment: How a discovered URL is classified into a surface: substring match on the path.

templates._comment: URL-shaped surfaces, addressed by the first label of the domain.

channels._comment: Surfaces the engine already knows how to fetch, named here rather than re-implemented. The walk decides when to ask; discover.py knows how.

ats._comment: Applicant-tracking boards are only readable through their JSON APIs. The HTML boards lie: jobs.ashbyhq.com answers HTTP 200 for a slug that does not exist, so a status check reports 'board found' for every company forever, and apply.workable.com serves a named board page for accounts with zero postings. One company in eight in the probe had a board at all, which is why hiring is evidence a lane asks for, never evidence a lane assumes.

removed._comment: Surfaces that were in the guess-list and are not any more, with the reason they went. Kept as a record so nobody re-adds them from memory.
removed./customers: 404 on 8 of 8 domains, each returning that domain's own error template.
removed.jobs.lever.co/<slug> (HTML board): 404 on 8 of 8, and the missing-slug baseline is 404 too. The JSON API is the readable form and is kept.
removed.boards.greenhouse.io/<slug> (HTML board): The board host moved to job-boards.greenhouse.io. The JSON API is kept.
removed.clutch.co/profile/<slug>: HTTP 403 on 8 of 8 domains, flat, with no challenge page. A surface that never answers is not a source.
removed.bluesky (public search): app.bsky.feed.searchPosts answered HTTP 403 on both public hosts, 2026-09. app.bsky.actor.searchActors answers 200 but returns accounts, which is a name match rather than evidence of work.
removed.youtube transcripts: The watch page lists captionTracks, but every timedtext fetch returns HTTP 200 with a zero-length body: proof-of-origin gating. Reading transcripts now needs a client that implements POT (yt-dlp), which is not a dependency here.
removed.x.com / twitter: Paid API; no keyless read path.
removed.linkedin: robots.txt disallows the job paths and pages answer 403.

vendor_stories._comment: Independent prose about an entity, published by the vendor it works with — and, now that the review directories refuse automated access, the half of the tier-1 evidence gate that review sites used to supply. Enumerated rather than searched: walk each vendor's sitemap index one level, keep the story paths, fetch the pages, and let attribution file each story under the entity it names.

community._comment: The social and community channels that do answer, each through its own API rather than an HTML scrape: Hacker News (Algolia), Reddit (archive + RSS), Stack Exchange (api.stackexchange), dev.to, Lobsters, Lemmy. Stack Overflow serves 403 to every plain fetch, so its questions are read through the API.
